I loved D&D when I was younger. Then something changed in me and I started looking for something more in RPGs. Like you, the randomness didn't always work for me, and I wasn't very competitive or that concerned with tactics. I wanted to play in worlds I invented, and in all sorts of genre and mixed genre (spy, space, robots, fantasy, horror, cowboy-horror). D&D also had a lot of rules that always needed tweaking to make game play enjoyable for our group. I also had more interest in the story part of the game, in creating and playing heroic characters, D&D didn't do a lot to encourage this sort of play -- I mean the players could go there, but the game mechanics didn't embrace the story.

I went from D&D and a bunch of other similar games, to Gurps. I liked Gurps because it was generic, but it still suffered playability issues. Too many rules to learn and fuss with, and not enough focus on story. Then I went to Fudge. It was simple, free, and pretty cool. The simplicity allowed us to focus on the story. Later I found Fate, which is based on Fudge. It's very story focused, light on rules, and fun to play!

I highly advise checking out role playing in general. Maybe look at attending a role playing convention with some buddies!

You have to be with a good group of people to truly get the best out of D&D and Pathfinder. If you're with people that aren't good sports it can be a horrible experience. Right now I play with my Dad, little brother, and boyfriend and it's a really great group.
